# Authoring requirements

This Skill guides the design, writing and review of model-facing instructions. Its host owns the deliverable and actual actions. Preserve the user's requested scope, including discussion-only and review-only tasks. Use simple, decision-useful language with no redundant ceremony or workflow. Judge necessity and instruction ownership before polishing text. Do not treat a bad result as proof of a cause or an effective method as necessarily mandatory. Preserve explicit results, permissions, useful domain context and intentional freedom. Apply this same specification to every model-facing file of the Skill, without exemption. Behavioral claims need observed evidence and causal claims need a controlled comparison. Improve supported defects, not arbitrary style preferences; retain the seven-file package unless a concrete task requires otherwise.

sources.used: Plain language, precise verbs, instruction-priority diagnosis and verification proportional to actual changes. No unverified model benchmark or historical lean-prompt metric adopted.
Decision value, retaining useful orientation and deleting redundant guidance. Repository-only ownership and initializer rules are not adopted as universal policy.
Find the actual behavior owner rather than infer it from where a symptom appears. Its .NET-specific commands and workflows are not copied.
Small high-signal context without brittle over-specification or vague high-level instructions; examples can carry needed information. This supports a design choice, not a measured effect here.

controls: no network/MCP/product actions authorized to evaluating model
environment.limitations: Default Codex host instructions can still apply; this is not an empty-system-prompt or automatic-selection evaluation.

metrics.measurement: Physical lines and Unicode character count including metadata. Neither tokenizer measurement nor proof of behavioral efficiency.
